text:
maya: Heads-up — since the v2.7 runtime canary rolled at ~09:10 we see p95 and p99 jumps on text-gen routes for a subset of customers. p50 is fine. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/abc
kevin: Can you paste the exact service and timeframe? p95 across all models or one model family?

maya: Model family = redwood-v1 / long-context routes (>=1024 tokens). Time window 09:10->09:40. p95 ~ 2.2s -> 3.8s, p99 5.1s -> 9.3s. Affected region: us-west-2.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout v2.7 -> runtime-node-3 (canary 10% traffic) started by @taylor at 2025-10-02T09:08:54Z (PR #4127)

taylor: I can roll the canary back if needed. wanted to validate KV cache refactor and new kernel selection heuristics.

jordan: Is this correlated with GPU utilization or queueing? Any change in batch sizes?

maya: GPU util stable. But queue length (requests waiting for batch) spiked 3x for canary nodes. Traces show long wait in batching layer.

kevin: Ok. sounds like batching heuristics regressed for long-context. Could be new sequence-length-aware binning. Can we reproduce locally with a load test that mimics long-context 128/512/2048 mix?

maya: Repro steps I ran:
```
# simple repro against canary gateway
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"'$(python -c "print('x'*1200)")'","max_tokens":64}' &
done
```
Result: median latency 1.9s, p99 ~8.7s. Running same against stable runtime returns p99 ~2.1s.

oncall: Paging @kevin and @taylor — customer escalations started. PD incident channel created.

taylor: Running a focused bisect: PR 4090..PR 4127 changed batching config + kernel selection. I'll bisect the commits on runtime branch to narrow to suspect.

kevin: In parallel, let's do quick mitigation: reduce canary traffic back to 0% (pause rollout) and shift users to stable. taylor can you run:
```
# emergency route command
redwoodctl rollout pause --canary v2.7
redwoodctl route set --service text-gen --split stable=100,canary=0
```
If that drops p99 back we're safe to bisect.

taylor: Pausing canary now. Executing route set... done. canary -> 0%.

maya: Confirming customer p99 back to baseline within 2 windows. Looks like traffic change fixed immediate impact.

kevin: Good. Now we need to find root cause before reintroducing changes. Maya — can you and jordan capture detailed traces of requests that hit canary nodes before rollback? We need batching logs, kernel selection decisions, sequence-length histograms, and any warnings.

maya: I already pulled a few traces. Example excerpt:
```
TRACE ID: trc-01F8
route: text-gen
node: runtime-node-3-canary
batch_wait_ms: 520
batch_size: 2
selected_kernel: aten_quant_v2
kv_cache_hit: false
notes: fallback to small-batch path
```
Pattern: many requests batched size 1-2 at 500ms wait, not aggregated. stable nodes had batch_size 8-12 and wait 80ms.

jordan: That suggests the new binning puts long-context requests into a path that expects fewer parallelizable requests, starving batching. Maybe the seq-length bin threshold off by factor (1024 vs 2048). I want to repro a small unit test that shows bin mismatch.

kevin: Also check the rollout config in PR 4127 for default batch timeouts and adaptive window changes. PR note said "decrease max_batch_delay to reduce latency for short requests" — maybe that reduced aggressiveness for long requests too.

maya: Found config snippet in PR 4127:
```
# runtime config
sequence_bins: [0-128,129-512,513-1024,1025-4096]
max_batch_delay_ms: {small:12, medium:20, large:50}
```
But the new code maps 1024->'medium' instead of 'large' due to off-by-one using <= vs <. So requests with length 1024 get medium delay and never wait long enough to form full batches.

taylor: Nice catch. That would increase batch_wait and smaller batches for long contexts. Fix is trivial — adjust comparator and add unit test. I'll open hotfix PR and run canary with small sample first. PR: #4132.

support-bot: Several customers notified via support ticket IDs: 88712, 88715. Escalation severity: P2.

kevin: While taylor prepares fix, we should add a temporary mitigation: for long-context routes force them to use the legacy binning via per-route override. Command:
```
redwoodctl config set --route text-gen --override sequence_bins=legacy
```
That reduces risk of reintroducing regression to other models.

taylor: Hotfix PR #4132 created, includes unit test for sequence bin boundaries and integration test with load harness. Running CI now.

maya: Re-running small canary with fix branch locally shows p99 drop to ~2.3s for the long-context load. Need full canary run.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollout v2.7-hotfix (canary 5%) triggered by @taylor at 2025-10-02T10:15:12Z (PR #4132)

jordan: Monitor queue length, batch_size, and kernel selections for next 20m. Also watch for any regressions on short-context routes (we changed comparator behavior).

maya: After 12m: canary hotfix nodes batch_size median 9, batch_wait 95ms, p99 ~2.4s. No new errors observed.

kevin: Good. Let's keep canary at 5% for 1h, then 25% if stable. Documented follow-ups:
- Add e2e test in CI that runs mixed-token-length harness.
- Improve telemetry: add per-bin pXX metrics and alert on unexpected drop in batch_size.
- Postmortem with timeline, root cause (off-by-one comparator), rollouts and mitigations.

taylor: I'll merge hotfix after 1h of stable canary. I'll also add stricter code review checklist for batching/selection logic.

maya: For support — reply to customers that we identified a batching bug in the canary runtime and we've paused the rollout and applied a hotfix to canary; stable nodes unaffected and we rolled back traffic.

oncall: Thanks all. Assigning oncall to run the postmortem doc. ping @kevin for follow-up owner. :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks for fast triage everyone.

maya: closing the thread after we've merged and observed 4h stable metrics.

oncall: Incident channel will remain open for 24h. If anything pops, re-open.
